newsitem.title: PERU: Peru guerrilla leader wanted exile in Cuba - tapes.
newsitem.headline: Peru guerrilla leader wanted exile in Cuba - tapes.

text.p: Peruvian Marxist guerrilla leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini, killed in the storming of the Japanese ambassador's residence, wanted to accept an offer of exile in Cuba, according to tape recordings published this week.

But the conversations, given by police to the opposition Caretas magazine, which is published on Thursdays, showed Cerpa was voted down 3-1 by his co-leaders to maintain their stand at the residence where they held 72 hostages for four months.
He and 13 other Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels died in the April 22 military assault that freed all the captives except one, who died in the attack.

According to a conversation three days before the assault, secretly recorded by receivers smuggled into the residence, Cerpa urged his sub-commanders to accept an offer of exile from Cuban President Fidel Castro.

"It is necessary to subject ourselves to the concrete conditions of the situation," he said. "Let's accept going with all our companions in this residence. Everything is arranged with the Cuban government, also (Peruvian President Alberto) Fujimori's government is promising us an amnesty, and I believe him."

But a rebel named "Tito," opposing Cerpa at various points in the dialogue, interrupted to say: "Comrade ... MRTA supporters expect more of you. The people and our supporters will not see our exile as an alternative strategy but as a capitulation."

The recordings also showed that Cerpa anticipated a military rescue, and that "Tito" suspected Roman Catholic archbishop Juan Luis Cipriani, mediating on behalf of the Vatican, of spying for the government.
"I have always considered him a spy. I hope I'm wrong," said "Tito" according to the tapes, which could not be independently verified but were widely accepted in Peru to be true.
It is still unknown how Peru's security forces managed to plant bugs and cameras inside the residence, with some versions saying Cipriani brought them in a Bible and a crucifix.
